o: Filter the global finishing order down to just your friends' IDs, preserving relative order. Example 1: order [3,1,2,5,4], friends {1,3,4} → [3,1,4]. With n ≤ 100 and ≤ 8 friends, anything linear works; a set membership test is the cleanest.
k: One pass over order, keeping entries whose ID is in the friends set.
Set lookup makes the filter O(n + f).

a.i: Put friends into a set, then stream through order emitting IDs present in the set. Relative finishing order is preserved automatically.
s: Scan order; append IDs found in the set.
a.t: O(n + f) — one pass with O(1) lookups.

a.i: Build rank[id] = finishing position from order, then sort friends by their ranks. Equivalent result, useful when friends arrive unsorted or you need positions.
a.t: O(n + f log f) — ranking pass plus sorting the friends.

w: The set-filter is simplest and optimal; the rank-sort variant generalizes to unsorted friend lists. No real pitfalls at this scale. Follow-up: top-k friends by finish position, or streaming finish events.
